newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end lower on week's last session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end lower on week's last session.

text.p: Argentine stocks shed some ground Wednesday as players reduced their exposure ahead of the Easter break Thursday and Friday, dealers said.

"Investors preferred to stay liquid since Wall Street stays open Thursday and there is a prevailing sense of uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy after yesterday's hike," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
The Fed raised short-term rates by 25 basis points Tuesday and analysts said other small hikes may be in store near-term.
The blue-chip MerVal index fell 0.7 percent to 739.15, paring the week's gains to 1.2 percent.
"We had risen in the previous five sessions so you could call it normal profit-taking," Bonanno said.
He predicted the MerVal could correct downwards to 730 points early next week before turning positive again.
Traders noted the U.S. long bond yield closed at 6.99 percent Wednesday, just below the psychological mark of 7.0 percent.

"Things aren't working out quite the way we expected -- the U.S. markets apparently had digested the quarter-point rate hike but they're already worried about the next possible move by the Fed," another trader said.
The bolsa's all-share index matched MerVal losses of 0.7 percent Wednesday, with decliners beating risers 35 to 15 and 19 issues closing flat.
Floor volume shrank to 19.2 million from 29 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover fell to 137.4 million pesos from 172.4 million Tuesday.
Main-tier losses were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Sevel and steelmaker Siderca, which pulled back 2.7 percent, 2.7 percent and 2.2 percent respectively.

The only two MerVal risers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which tacked on 1.6 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively. Traders said Alpargatas rose on news of streamlining plans.
